summary: Kempshall Mountain lookout, Hamilton County NY: wooden tower 1911, 35-ft steel tower 1918, closed 1971, removed 1977 or 1980s; parts now an exhibit tower.

facts.design: 35-foot Aermotor LS40 steel tower, erected 1918, replacing a wooden tower from 1911
facts.status_note: The mountain tower was dismantled; parts went into an exhibit tower at the Adirondack History Museum in Elizabethtown.

access.note: The exhibit tower is climbed from inside the Adirondack History Museum; visitors must enter the museum to climb it.

visit.trail_note: The old state trail from Long Lake to the summit was left largely unmaintained after the tower came down; some old state trail markers remain along parts of it.

events.note: Wooden tower built by the Conservation Commission; the first structure on the summit.
A new observer cabin was placed on Kempshall Mountain as part of a set of seven.
A 35-foot Aermotor LS40 steel tower was bought and erected, replacing the wooden tower.
New cabins were built at Kempshall, per the 1925 Conservation Commission report.
The Civilian Conservation Corps built a new cabin for the observer's living quarters.
Fire lookout operations ended at the end of the 1971 season after aerial detection took over.
The steel tower was dismantled in June 1977, per the Adirondack Explorer. The NHLR says the 1980s.
The museum bought the tower parts and built one exhibit tower. NHLR says the 1990s; the exact year is not given.
Recorded by the National Historic Lookout Register on May 22, 2022, as US 1596, NY 48.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Adirondack Explorer says the steel tower was dismantled in June 1977; the NHLR says the Kempshall and West towers were removed in the 1980s. The sources are not reconciled; the story gives both.
Wikipedia places the mountain northwest of the hamlet of Long Lake; the Explorer says it rises on the northeast side of Long Lake. The story says near Long Lake and does not pick a side.
Wikipedia calls the exhibit's host the Essex County Historical Museum; the NHLR entry and the firelookout.org index name the Adirondack History Museum. The story uses the latter.

notes_for_editor: A separate record, us-ny-kempshall-mountain-at-adirondack-history-museum, already covers the exhibit tower; this story covers the original mountain and points to the museum. Not checked: a Lake Placid News item (search snippet only, not fetched, page-read cap reached) says the Historical Society bought two towers the DEC had dismantled in 1979, which conflicts with the NHLR's 1990s purchase. Worth a fetch before publishing. No observer names, staffing dates or fires were found in the pages read, so none are in the story. The NYSFFLA newsletter prints a Kempshall cabin photo credited to Percy Stanton (dated 1949/Model 1941) inside the PDF; there is no image URL, so it is not in photos. Museum hours were not re-checked this session.
